ticket.title: storypole handoff: populate the context packet from telemetry spans by task key
acceptance_criteria:
SCOPE 2026-11-07, from plans/GB-243.md section 12.3. Fourth runtime consumer.

WHAT: `storypole handoff <KEY>` currently asks the operator to summarise what happened. Populate the handoff packet from spans matching `task_key`: MCP tools called, files inspected, the last `outfeed gate` step statuses, wall time elapsed, and `sawhorse` tokens consumed.

WHY THIS IS THE HIGHEST-VALUE OF THE FOUR: a handoff is written exactly when an agent ran out of context or time, which is the moment a human summary is least reliable and most expensive. The spans already recorded every one of those facts truthfully; asking for them again is asking a tired process to remember what a file knows.

WHAT MUST NOT HAPPEN: the generated section must be distinguishable from what a human wrote. A handoff packet that silently mixes measured facts with recalled ones is worse than either alone, because the reader cannot tell which claims to trust. So the packet carries a clearly-labelled generated block with its provenance (span count, window, and the task key it filtered on).

HONEST EMPTINESS: if there are no spans for the key - the task predates the recorder, or was done in a terminal without telemetry - the block says so and says what that means, rather than rendering empty sections that read as "nothing happened".

MECHANISM NOTE: the packet is built by the CLI reading the sqlite index, so the same rules as GB-306 apply - a missing index, an empty window or a locked database degrades to "no generated section", never to a failed handoff. Handing off must not be blockable by an observability file.

Done when: a handoff for a task with recorded spans includes tools, files, gate statuses, elapsed wall time and tokens, labelled as generated with its provenance; a handoff for a task without spans says so explicitly; and neither case can fail the command.
